slides.title: JIT Compilation and Vectorization
slides.prompt: Numba uses LLVM to JIT-compile numerical Python/NumPy code directly to machine code at runtime. Vectorization processes arrays in SIMD blocks. PyPy replaces standard CPython with an alternative JIT-enabled interpreter.

slides.title: Numba JIT Decorator
slides.prompt: Fill in the primary Numba decorator used to JIT-compile standard numerical functions.

slides.title: Numba nopython Mode Equivalent
slides.prompt: Which shorthand decorator in Numba is equivalent to `@jit(nopython=True)` for maximum performance?

slides.title: Numba Vectorize Decorator
slides.prompt: Fill in the Numba decorator used to convert scalar functions into NumPy universal functions (ufuncs).

slides.title: PyPy Interpreter Nature
options: A fast, compliant alternative Python interpreter featuring a JIT (Just-In-Time) compiler
A C-extension wrapper library for C++ STL containers
A static linter for optimizing Python memory usage
A bytecode disassembler included in CPython standard library
slides.correctAnswer: A fast, compliant alternative Python interpreter featuring a JIT (Just-In-Time) compiler

slides.title: PyPy Compatibility Engine Target
slides.prompt: Fill in the standard CPython runtime implementation that PyPy aims to replace transparently.
slides.codeSnippet: PyPy provides a JIT compiler alternative to standard ___.

slides.title: JIT Fallback Mode Warning
slides.prompt: What happens in Numba when `nopython=False` and Numba cannot optimize a specific Python object or function?
options: It falls back to 'object mode', running via the CPython API with minimal speed gains
It raises a HardCompileError and halts program execution
It converts the script into C++ source files on disk
It automatically offloads execution to an attached GPU
slides.correctAnswer: It falls back to 'object mode', running via the CPython API with minimal speed gains
